claim: At its Capital Markets Day, whose call is on Friday 27 November 2026 at 10:00 CET, Rheinmetall cuts its 2030 group sales target below the "around €50bn" set in November 2025.

runs.reason:
**I forecast YES.** Rheinmetall is more likely to publish a lower 2030 group sales figure than to retain the €50 billion ambition or leave it unquantified.

**Base rate.** I’d start at roughly 25% for an industrial company to cut a one-year-old, long-term sales target at its next Capital Markets Day. That’s a judgmental prior, not a measured frequency. The closest company-specific precedent points the other way: Rheinmetall went from discussing €40–50 billion of 2030 sales potential before its November 2025 event to presenting around €50 billion at the event. ([ir.rheinmetall.com](https://ir.rheinmetall.com/media/document/35946ea5-5f30-4425-97f8-294d79f1c4d4/assets/Rheinmetall-Transcript-Conference-Call-2025-Q3.pdf?utm_source=openai))

**What moves this case above that prior.**
- **Toward YES — November 5:** Rheinmetall cut 2026 group sales guidance from €13.7–14.2 billion to around €13.2 billion. From that lower starting point, reaching €50 billion in 2030 would take roughly 40% annual sales growth over four years. The immediate delays don’t prove that sales are lost, but they make the existing ambition harder to defend. ([rheinmetall.com](https://www.rheinmetall.com/en/media/news-watch/news/2026/11/2026-11-05-rheinmetall-news-quarterly-statement-q3?utm_source=openai))
- **Toward YES — November 5:** Asked about the 2030 target, CFO Klaus Neumann said the figure and how the company intended to reach it would be a key part of the CMD presentation. That makes a numerical update more likely than silence, though it does not establish that the figure will be lower. ([earningscalls.dev](https://earningscalls.dev/transcripts/rheinmetall-ag_rhm_earnings_call_transcript_2026-11-05))
- **Toward NO — November 5:** Nine-month group sales rose 38%, and backlog reached €78 billion, up from €56.7 billion a year earlier. Management has a credible case that the latest setbacks shift revenue between years rather than reduce the long-term opportunity. ([rheinmetall.com](https://www.rheinmetall.com/en/media/news-watch/news/2026/11/2026-11-05-rheinmetall-news-quarterly-statement-q3?utm_source=openai))

**Window risk.** I put about 1% on the call not taking place within the window: the company lists a November 27 webcast at 10:00 CET, and November 25 reporting still shows that slot. The bigger risk to YES is that the event goes ahead but management gives only nearer-term or segment figures, or drops the €50 billion ambition without replacing it. ([rheinmetall.com](https://www.rheinmetall.com/en/investor-relations/calendar-and-events/capital-markets-day?cType=SocialRecruiting))

runs.reason:
Management stated during the Q3 update that 2027 and longer-term guidance, including growth targets and supporting milestones, would be addressed at the November CMD.
* **2026-11-05 to 2026-11-24 (Downward pressure - strong):** Following what was described as the fifth revenue or profit warning in 11 months and a >50% share price decline from January 2026 highs, management faces intense institutional pressure to reset targets to a credible, achievable level. Even if some delayed orders (like Arminius) are merely shifted into 2027, underperformance in joint ventures (such as Destinus), the lost F126 contract, and lower near-term CapEx make the €50 billion trajectory much harder to defend without modification.

**3. Strongest Reason the Obvious Outcome Might Fail**
There are two noteworthy ways a YES resolution could fail:
First, CEO Armin Papperger is historically known for bold, optimistic top-line communication and emphasized in July 2026 that the lost F126 contract represented less than 3% of the 2030 target, while the Arminius delay is primarily a timing shift from late 2026 into early 2027. With a record €78 billion backlog at the end of Q3 2026 (up 38% year-on-year), management might insist that the €50 billion ambition for 2030 remains intact, or present a wide range whose midpoint is still €50 billion.
Second, under the strict resolution criteria, if Rheinmetall decides to abandon or withdraw the 2030 target entirely in favor of shorter-term (e.g., 2027–2028) rolling guidance without stating a new numeric 2030 group sales figure, the question resolves NO. While the CMD event itself is actively underway in Hamburg (25–27 November, with the main webcast scheduled for 27 November at 10:00 CET), these two possibilities keep the probability from reaching certainty.

facts.fact: Rheinmetall guided during its Capital Markets Day presentation for annual group sales of around €50 billion and an operating margin of more than 20% by 2030.
Rheinmetall stated in an ad-hoc announcement that the canceled F126 frigate programme had a planned contribution of below 3% to its 2030 mid-term revenue guidance.

Rheinmetall lowered its 2026 sales outlook to €13.7 billion–€14.2 billion, cut its 2026 order book guidance from roughly €135 billion to more than €100 billion, and reduced its capital expenditure target from 16% to 8%–9% of sales.

Rheinmetall cut its 2026 revenue forecast to about €13.2 billion and its operating margin forecast to around 18.5% after delays to defence contracts and ammunition deliveries pushed expected revenue into 2027.

Rheinmetall reported that nine-month 2026 sales rose 38% year-on-year to €8.4 billion while operating free cash flow was €-1,698 million due to inventory build-up and project delays in the German armed forces' Arminius project.

Along with its Q3 2026 earnings release, Rheinmetall stated that lowered 2026 revenue and margin forecasts were also impacted by lower-than-expected revenue from new business activities, particularly its collaboration with Destinus.
Rheinmetall's order backlog stood at €78 billion after the first nine months of 2026 ahead of its Capital Markets Day in Hamburg on 26–27 November 2026.

runs.reason:
The Capital Markets Day call is on the calendar and inside the window, but a lower 2030 group sales figure is not yet in hand. Near-term misses and a stretched path from about €13bn make a reset plausible; silence or a reaffirmed “around €50bn” would still be NO.

Base rate: at a scheduled CMD, large European industrials often restate a medium-term ambition, but formally cutting a five-year sales ambition (as opposed to the current-year outlook) is only a minority outcome — on the order of two-fifths — because “around €X” language is soft and management can blame timing rather than demand.

What shifts this case: Rheinmetall has already cut 2026 sales twice (August, then 5 November, to about €13.2bn) and dropped the >40% cash-conversion aim, while the stock has repriced a much lower 2030 outcome. Getting from ~€13bn in 2026 to €50bn in 2030 still implies roughly 40% annual growth, and several houses have framed the Hamburg event as the moment for a rewrite. The incentive to put a credible number above what the market already discounts, but below €50bn, is real. Offsetting that, the November misses are described by the company as shifts (Arminius into 2027, slower ammunition acceptances), which move revenue into the 2030 window rather than out of it, and the 5 November release still called the growth path “solid and sustainable.” The €78bn backlog supports that story. Under the criterion, segment charts alone, a withdrawn target with no replacement, or any restatement of “around €50bn” or higher are all NO.
